title: KfW ERP Capital for Start-ups (Verified Example)
eligibility: Less than 3 years in operation. Registered in Germany. Solid business plan required.
verification_notes: Sourced manually from KfW's official 067 product detail page.
funding_objective: To fully finance the start-up phase via low-interest loans where KfW assumes 80% of the default risk, easing traditional bank requirements.
short_summary: An officially verified, state-backed start-up loan offering up to 500k to young companies with 80% risk assumption by KfW.
full_description: The ERP Start-up Loan Universal helps founders, freelancers and small enterprises that have been active in the market for less than 3 years to gain access to comprehensive funding. The unique aspect of the 067 mandate is the 80% risk assumption which incentivizes local commercial banks to process the loans smoothly.
application_process: Must be routed through the founder's commercial housebank. The housebank handles application to KfW.
required_documents: Comprehensive business plan, commercial registration, private credit check.
incubator_or_partner_support: Local Chamber of Commerce (IHK) advising recommended prior to bank meeting.

title: ZIM Innovation Grant for SMEs (Individual & Cooperation)
funding_amount: Typically 25%–60% of eligible project costs (max eligible cost €690,000 for individual projects)
eligibility: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Germany (under 250 employees) undertaking innovative, high-risk R&D projects with clear commercialization potential. Projects must demonstrate technological novelty beyond the current state of the art.
geographic_eligibility: Registered office, permanent establishment, or branch in Germany.
provider_organization: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK)
verification_notes: Based on publicly available ZIM programme documentation. Maximum eligible project cost for individual projects referenced as €690,000; exact conditions may vary by project type and guideline updates.
funding_objective: To increase the innovative capacity and competitiveness of SMEs and support market-oriented R&D projects.
short_summary: A non-repayable, multi-sector R&D grant for SMEs covering a percentage of eligible project costs under Germany’s ZIM programme.
full_description: ZIM (Zentrales Innovationsprogramm Mittelstand) is a central innovation funding programme of the German Federal Government aimed at strengthening the innovative capacity of SMEs. It supports individual and cooperative R&D projects with non-repayable grants. Funding rates depend on company size, project type, and location, typically ranging from 25% to 60% of eligible costs. The programme is technology- and industry-neutral and focuses on market-oriented innovation.
application_process: Applications can be submitted continuously. Projects should not begin before approval. Applications must include detailed project and commercialization plans.
required_documents: Detailed project description, innovation justification, commercialization plan, and financial projections.
incubator_or_partner_support: Cooperation with research institutions and partners is supported under cooperative project formats.

title: EXIST Start-up Grant (EXIST-Gründerstipendium)
funding_amount: Monthly stipend (approx. €1,000–€3,000 per founder) plus additional material and coaching support
eligibility: Students, graduates, and researchers from universities or research institutions in Germany planning to start an innovative, technology- or knowledge-based business. The project must be supported by a university or research institution.
geographic_eligibility: Project must be associated with a German university or research institution.
provider_organization: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK)
verification_notes: Based on official EXIST programme information. Funding includes monthly stipends and additional project costs; exact amounts vary depending on applicant role and project needs.
funding_objective: To support the creation of innovative, knowledge-based start-ups emerging from universities and research institutions in Germany.
short_summary: A government-funded stipend programme supporting students and researchers in launching innovative start-ups from academic institutions.
full_description: The EXIST Start-up Grant (EXIST-Gründerstipendium) supports students, graduates, and researchers in preparing innovative business start-ups. Funding is provided as a monthly stipend for founders, along with additional resources for materials, coaching, and startup development. The programme focuses on technology-oriented or knowledge-based business ideas and requires support from a university or research institution.
application_process: Applications must be submitted through a university or research institution. The institution evaluates and forwards the application to the programme authorities.
required_documents: Business concept, innovation description, team profile, and confirmation of support from a university or research institution.
incubator_or_partner_support: Strong support from university incubators, mentors, and research institutions is required.

title: NRW.BANK Start-up and Growth Loan (Gründung und Wachstum)
eligibility: Startups (less than 5 years old), SMEs, and freelancers seeking to invest or cover working capital for projects located in North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW).
verification_notes: Verified max funding at 10 million EUR via official NRW.BANK guidelines. Exact interest rates fluctuate and are individually determined by house-banks.
funding_objective: To provide highly subsidized growth capital and start-up financing for foundational investments in North Rhine-Westphalia.
short_summary: A state-backed loan up to €10 million for start-ups and SMEs in NRW, featuring discounted interest rates and a 50% liability release option.
full_description: The NRW.BANK.Gründung und Wachstum (Start-up and Growth) program provides comprehensive financing for foundational investments and working capital. The maximum loan amount is €10 million, effectively covering up to 100% of eligible costs. Young companies active for less than 5 years receive heavily discounted interest rates fixed for up to 10 years. An optional 50% indemnification (liability release) mitigates risk for the commercial house-bank, easing the approval process.
application_process: Applications must be submitted via the founder's commercial bank (Hausbankverfahren), which acts as the intermediary to NRW.BANK. Must apply before the project starts.
required_documents: Comprehensive business plan, proof of commercial qualification, and secured overall project financing.
incubator_or_partner_support: Local Chamber of Commerce (IHK) or Chamber of Crafts (HWK) consultation is highly recommended prior to application.
